$description: Nexus Cyberdeck design tokens. This file is the source of truth: packages/tokens/src/tokens.css and src/contrast.gen.ts are both generated from it by `npm run build:tokens`. Do not edit either of those by hand. Format is W3C DTCG ($value/$type/$description), so Style Dictionary v4+ and Figma/Tokens Studio can read it unchanged; the only project-specific addition is the $extensions block described on each token that uses one.

primitive.$description: Raw values. Never referenced by a component — the semantic layer below is the only surface components may use, and lint enforces it.

panel.$description: Panel surface. Every contrast ratio in this system is measured against this colour.

alarm.$description: RESTRICTED. Reachable only through semantic.fg.critical. Spending this on a button is what collapses the whole language — the magenta reads as a warning precisely because nothing else uses it.

ramp.$description: Muted grey ramp, solved rather than eyeballed: hue 100deg, saturation 13%, binary-searched per step against exact contrast targets. The two steps that carry a WCAG floor are solved against primitive.colour.raised, the lightest opaque background in the system, so the floor holds on every surface a component can render on rather than only on the panel the quoted ratios are measured against. Theme-scoped — $value is the default (hud-aa) and $extensions carries the other theme, which is how a DTCG consumer still reads a correct default.

grey-200.$description: UI boundary — target 3.0 for WCAG 1.4.11, on the raised surface.

grey-300.$description: Disabled text — target 4.5 for WCAG 1.4.3, on the raised surface.

stencil.$value: Impact, Haettenschweiler, "Arial Narrow Bold", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif

scale.$description: Per-theme type scale multiplier. Every size below is emitted as calc(base * var(--nx-font-scale)), so the whole scale moves with the theme.

text.$description: Base type sizes in rem, before the theme's font-scale is applied. Emitted as calc() so browser zoom and user font-size preferences keep working — WCAG 1.4.4.

blink.$description: ~0.94Hz. Capped here, not in the component: WCAG 2.3.1 Level A prohibits flashing above 3Hz. The prototype blinked at 9Hz.

z.$description: Stacking order for the fixed/absolute overlays, relative only to one another. Each is a plain number, not a colour or dimension, so it is used directly rather than through the semantic layer — the same treatment primitive.motion and primitive.shape already get. A component that establishes its own stacking context (an ancestor with transform, filter, perspective, a non-visible contain, or opacity below 1) resets this scale for everything inside it; see packages/react/README.md for the 'no transformed ancestor' constraint that follows from position: fixed.

z-drawer.$description: Drawer. A persistent panel, not modal — sits under a tooltip that points at something inside it, and under the command palette's scrim.

z-tooltip.$description: Tooltip. Transient, follows the pointer, so it outranks the persistent Drawer panel.

z-overlay.$description: CommandPalette's scrim and panel. Modal — the highest layer, above everything else including an open Drawer.

crt.$description: Primitives for the opt-in crt.css layer.

semantic.$description: Roles. The only names a component may reference. Every name exists in both themes, so switching theme never touches component code.

track.$description: Unfilled ground of a meter/progress track. Deliberately neutral rather than phosphor-tinted: it sits under an arbitrary category colour, and a green cast would shift every one of them.

cat-lime.$description: Categorical slot — carries no status meaning. Exists so code encoding arbitrary categories has a named handle instead of reaching into the primitive layer.

default.$description: Decorative hairline. Exempt from the non-text floor through the nexus.contrast extension: at 1.61:1 it has never met 3.0, and semantic.border.strong is the role that carries a control's boundary and is held to it. Whether a control identifiable by this hairline alone is a 1.4.11 failure is a separate question from this exemption.

strong.$description: UI boundary. Held to the theme's non-text floor on every opaque surface.

split.$description: Chromatic split for display type. Lighter than the crt pair, which composites over a whole surface rather than fringing a single glyph.

focus.$description: WCAG 2.4.7. Applied globally in base.css and not removable per-component.

theme.$description: Themes are not tokens; they name which override set applies. Every colour in primitive.colour is identical across both — only the muted ramp and the type scale move, which is why the accessible theme needed no redesign.

hud.label: Prototype
hud.note: The PoC verbatim. Muted text fails AA. Ship only where the operator opts into an immersive surface.
